items.title: Sandflare – I built a sandbox that launches AI agent VMs in ~300ms
items.raw_excerpt: I've been building Sandflare for the past few months — it launches Firecracker microVMs for AI agents in ~300ms cold start. The idea came from running LLM-generated code in production. Docker felt too risky (shared kernel), full VMs too slow (5–10s). Firecracker hits the middle: real VM isolation, fast boot. I also added managed Postgres because almost every agent I built needed persistent state. One call wires a database into a sandbox. There are great tools in this space already (E2B, Modal, Daytona) — I wanted something with batteries-included Postgres, and simpler pricing What I'm trying to figure out: how do I get cold start below 100ms? Currently the bottleneck is the Firecracker API + network setup. Would love to hear from anyone who's pushed Firecracker further. https://sandflare.i

excerpt_i18n.en: On March 31, ByteDance's AI programming product TRAE launched the "SOLO Standalone Edition." The original SOLO mode (SOLO Agent) was deeply integrated into traditional IDE architectures. The release of the SOLO Standalone Edition aims to optimize the onboarding experience for new users, reduce the learning curve and usage barriers associated with IDE environments, and extend the SOLO mode from programming to broader productivity scenarios. Building on the core Agent capabilities of the original PC-based SOLO mode, the new SOLO Standalone Edition includes both desktop and web versions, each offering two functional modes: Code and MTC (More Than Coding). Through a lighter and more intuitive interaction paradigm, it provides users with an immersive and efficient AI-driven development experience. The Code mode primarily targets code development scenarios, incorporating the core capabilities of SOLO Agent and a more streamlined tool panel, mainly catering to developers accustomed to Agent-led development. In Code mode, the SOLO Standalone Edition enables collaboration between the desktop and web versions: when a user creates a Remote task in the SOLO desktop version, the web version synchronously opens and shares the task in real time. Users can monitor task progress on other device terminals, and tasks will not stop due to computer sleep. More Than Cod
excerpt_i18n.es: El 31 de marzo, TRAE, el producto de programación con IA de ByteDance, lanzó la "versión independiente SOLO". El modo SOLO original (SOLO Agent) de TRAE estaba profundamente integrado en la arquitectura tradicional de IDE. Con el lanzamiento de esta versión independiente, se busca optimizar la experiencia inicial de los nuevos usuarios, reducir la curva de aprendizaje y las barreras de uso asociadas al entorno IDE, y extender el modo SOLO desde el ámbito de la programación a escenarios de productividad más amplios. Basándose en las capacidades centrales del Agente del modo SOLO en la versión original para PC, la nueva versión independiente SOLO incluye dos formatos: aplicación de escritorio y versión web, ambos ofreciendo Cod.

excerpt_i18n.en: In recent days, TurboQuant has become one of the hottest controversies in the AI academic community. On one side, Google Research has prominently published a blog post, presenting it as a "breakthrough" work that significantly reduces the inference costs of large models and is set to debut at ICLR 2026. On the other side, Gao Jianyang, the author of the prior work RaBitQ, has publicly criticized the paper on the Zhihu platform, with his latest post updated in the early hours of March 30. He argues that the paper has serious issues in its method description, theoretical comparisons, and experimental disclosures. This Zhihu post has already garnered nearly 5K upvotes. In just a few days, the dispute has evolved beyond technical discussion into a public tug-of-war over originality attribution, paper narrative, and the academic influence of major tech companies. To clarify the issues with TurboQuant, the external criticism of Google in this controversy is not just a vague "similarity" claim. Public comments have specifically focused on three points: first, whether TurboQuant deliberately downplayed its methodological connections to RaBitQ; second, whether the paper's characterization of RaBitQ's theory as "suboptimal" is justified; and third, whether the experimental comparisons were set up to favor TurboQuant while disadvantaging prior work. These remain points of public debate, not formal judgments, but they indicate that from the outset, this controversy is not merely about "missing citations" but strikes at the very core of academic research.

Por otro lado, Gao Jianyang, autor del trabajo previo RaBitQ, criticó duramente en la comunidad como usuario de Zhihu, con su última actualización en la madrugada del 30 de marzo, señalando graves problemas en la descripción del método, comparaciones teóricas y divulgación experimental. Esta publicación en Zhihu ya ha recibido cerca de 5.000 "me gusta". En pocos días, esta controversia ha ido más allá.

items.raw_excerpt: OpenClaw 的爆火，让一个原本更多停留在技术圈内部的变化，突然变得具象起来。 当一个 Agent 可以跨应用执行任务、调用工具、在几乎没有人工干预的情况下完成复杂流程时，人们第一次直观地看到：AI 正在从“生成内容的工具”，转变为“参与行动的主体”。也正是在这一刻，安全问题迅速被推到前台。 但一个更值得注意的现象是，在几乎所有关于 Agent 安全的讨论中，问题的定义仍然高度集中在模型层面：输入是否被注入、输出是否越界、对齐是否失效。这种讨论路径本身并没有错，但它隐含着一个前提，即安全问题主要发生在“模型”这一单点之上。 问题在于，这个前提可能正在失效。当 Agent 不再只是响应指令，而是持续接收来自不同来源的信息、在多组件结构中做出决策、并通过工具链将决策转化为现实动作时，“安全”所指向的对象，已经不再是单一模型，而是一个由模型、记忆、工具、环境以及交互链路共同构成的系统。 在这样的系统中，风险不一定以“错误输出”的形式出现，也不一定以“瞬时失控”的方式爆发。它可能表现为决策过程中的偏移、信息在链路中的传递与放大，甚至是跨组件、跨主体之间的相互影响。 这也意味着，Agent 安全的问题，正在从“是否安全”，转向“如何被影响”。 在论文《From Secure Agentic AI to Secure Agentic Web》中，上海交通大学、上海创智学院张伟楠团队正是从这一转变出发，尝试将 Agent 安全从模型层面的鲁棒性问题，重新置于系统结构与运行机制之中进行讨论。 围绕这一问题，AI 科技评论与论文一作邓智航进行了对话。下文在不改变原意的前提下，对访谈内容进行了整理与呈现，试图还原其对于 Agent 安全问题“从模型走向系统”的整体理解。 论文链接：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.01564 Agent 安全，被理解错了吗？ AI 科技

excerpt_i18n.zh: OpenClaw 的爆火，让一个原本更多停留在技术圈内部的变化，突然变得具象起来。 当一个 Agent 可以跨应用执行任务、调用工具、在几乎没有人工干预的情况下完成复杂流程时，人们第一次直观地看到：AI 正在从“生成内容的工具”，转变为“参与行动的主体”。也正是在这一刻，安全问题迅速被推到前台。 但一个更值得注意的现象是，在几乎所有关于 Agent 安全的讨论中，问题的定义仍然高度集中在模型层面：输入是否被注入、输出是否越界、对齐是否失效。这种讨论路径本身并没有错，但它隐含着一个前提，即安全问题主要发生在“模型”这一单点之上。 问题在于，这个前提可能正在失效。当 Agent 不再只是响应指令，而是持续接收来自不同来源的信息、在多组件结构中做出决策、并通过工具链将决策转化为现实动作时，“安全”所指向的对象，已经不再是单一模型，而是一个由模型、记忆、工具、环境以及交互链路共同构成的系统。 在这样的系统中，风险不一定以“错误输出”的形式出现，也不一定以“瞬时失控”的方式爆发。它可能表现为决策过程中的偏移、信息在链路中的传递与放大，甚至是跨组件、跨主体之间的相互影响。 这也意味着，Agent 安全的问题，正在从“是否安全”，转向“如何被影响”。 在论文《From Secure Agentic AI to Secure Agentic Web》中，上海交通大学、上海创智学院张伟楠团队正是从这一转变出发，尝试将 Agent 安全从模型层面的鲁棒性问题，重新置于系统结构与运行机制之中进行讨论。 围绕这一问题，AI 科技评论与论文一作邓智航进行了对话。下文在不改变原意的前提下，对访谈内容进行了整理与呈现，试图还原其对于 Agent 安全问题“从模型走向系统”的整体理解。 论文链接：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.01564 Agent 安全，被理解错了吗？ AI 科技
excerpt_i18n.en:
The explosive popularity of OpenClaw has suddenly made tangible a change that was previously confined mostly within tech circles. When an agent can execute tasks across applications, call tools, and complete complex workflows with almost no human intervention, people see firsthand that AI is shifting from a "tool for generating content" to an "agent of action." It is precisely at this moment that security concerns are thrust into the spotlight.

However, a more noteworthy phenomenon is that in almost all discussions about agent security, the definition of the problem remains highly concentrated at the model level: whether inputs are being injected, outputs are exceeding boundaries, or alignment is failing. This line of discussion is not wrong in itself, but it implies a premise that security issues primarily occur at the single point of the "model."

The problem is that this premise may be becoming obsolete. When an agent no longer merely responds to instructions but continuously receives information from various sources, makes decisions within a multi-component structure, and translates those decisions into real-world actions through a toolchain, the focus of "security" is no longer a single model but a system composed of models, memory, tools, environment, and interaction pathways.

In such a system, risks may not manifest as "incorrect outputs" or erupt as "instantaneous loss of control." They could appear as deviations in the decision-making process, the transmission and amplification of information along pathways, or even interactions across components and agents.

excerpt_i18n.es: El éxito explosivo de OpenClaw ha hecho tangible un cambio que antes se limitaba principalmente al ámbito tecnológico. Cuando un Agente puede ejecutar tareas entre aplicaciones, invocar herramientas y completar procesos complejos con mínima intervención humana, la gente ve por primera vez de manera directa cómo la IA está pasando de ser una "herramienta que genera contenido" a un "sujeto que participa en acciones". Es precisamente en este momento cuando los problemas de seguridad saltan rápidamente al primer plano. Sin embargo, un fenómeno aún más notable es que, en casi todas las discusiones sobre la seguridad de los Agentes, la definición del problema sigue centrándose en gran medida en el nivel del modelo: si la entrada ha sido inyectada, si la salida excede los límites, o si la alineación se ha perdido.

Estos fondos se destinarán principalmente a tres áreas clave: investigación y desarrollo de tecnología central, expansión de la matriz de productos y despliegue de canales globales. Con la salud como campo estratégico, la compañía, apoyándose en el doble motor de "IA + audio" y su capacidad de ingeniería madura, acelera la construcción de un ecosistema de bienestar y comodidad que abarca dispositivos portátiles inteligentes, hardware innovador de IA y salud integral. excerpt_i18n.en:
I don't think an AI agent is a living entity or a digital twin; it's more like a superorganism. When discussing the future form of agents, Frank offered a rather sci-fi perspective. In his view, people have traditionally seen AI as a tool or a "digital twin" of humans, but with the advancement of agent technology, this understanding may soon become outdated. As early as last year, we had an in-depth conversation with Frank about various concepts related to agents. Frank holds a unique position in the AI community: on one hand, he is active in major offline tech gatherings, maintaining an almost instinctive excitement and curiosity about any technological developments; on the other hand, he has never stepped away from the technical front lines and is currently fully dedicated to an overseas acceleration and incubation project called "QLab."

In fact, Frank is better known to the public for his self-operated WeChat public account—AI Outlier Frank. When asked about the origin of "AI Outlier," Frank admitted that he aspires to be an "Outlier" in the AI era: to seek anomalies and become a new variable. In his view, unique and heterogeneous taste will be the most scarce resource in the future.

Frank attends offline AI events. This time, we met at a café. The interview lasted an hour and a half, and as it approached 11:30 a.m., he hurriedly got up to head to the next offline AI event for a presentation—a pace that has become almost routine for him lately.
excerpt_i18n.es: Creo que el agente de IA no es un ser vivo ni un doble, sino que se asemeja más a un supercuerpo. Al hablar sobre la forma futura de los agentes, Frank ofreció un juicio con un toque de ciencia ficción. En su opinión, la gente solía entender la IA como una herramienta o un "doble digital" humano, pero con el avance de la tecnología de agentes, esta comprensión podría quedar obsoleta pronto. Ya desde el año pasado, mantuvimos conversaciones profundas con Frank sobre diversas ideas relacionadas con los agentes. La identidad de Frank en el círculo de la IA es bastante particular: por un lado, es activo en grandes reuniones técnicas presenciales, manteniéndose al tanto de cualquier novedad tecnológica.
